newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Former Suncorp directors quit B of Q.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Former Suncorp directors quit B of Q.

text.p: Former Suncorp chairman Graham Tucker and his former deputy Ted Ranson have resigned as Bank of Queensland directors ahead of the bank's annual meeting next month, the Courier-Mail newspaper reported on Wednesday.
Suncorp chief executive Bernard Rowley had also submitted his resignation from the Bank of Queensland, effective November 30, the report said.
Bank of Queensland is 44 percent-owned by the Queensland state government which is merging Suncorp with Metway Bank Ltd and the Queensland Industry Development Corp (QIDC).
The resignation of Tucker and Ranson follows threats by the State Government to seek their removal from the Bank of Queensland board next month.
Both Tucker and Ranson along with fellow Suncorp director John Wruck resigned last month from the Suncorp board after expressing dissatisfaction over the government's planned merger.
The State Government subsequently had proposed three new directors to replace Tucker, Ranson and Rowley on the Bank of Queensland board.

Bank of Queensland chairman Neil Roberts, who has publicly distanced his bank from the merger arrangements, paid tribute to the contributions of each of the three directors, the newspaper report said.
"They leave the board knowing their efforts have seen the bank become a significant participant in financial services in Queensland," he said.
